answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on its backs, remove cards targeting colors not playing, and keep their own Ambush card. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “upright in its plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center; keep their values hidden.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player voting turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No. Red is the Target because Red has the most votes. A majority is not required; the player or players receiving the most votes are Targets, with all tied for most also being Targets.
answers.evidence: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. Since neither successfully Ambushed, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to any applicable Ambush effects.
answers.evidence: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; with tied Targets, “voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.” Targets are eliminated unless protected by their own successful Ambush.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue, and did not Ambush. Receiving no votes does not itself keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,” subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so Red has one counted vote (Yellow's) and Yellow has one (Pink's). Red and Yellow tie for most and are both Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds, so Red survives and may eliminate one player who voted for Red; the only such player is Yellow, whom Red eliminates. Pink voted for a tied Target (Yellow), so Pink survives. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: The illustrated vote states: “Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.”

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambusher chooses one player who voted for them to eliminate, not all four. They cannot choose a player who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: A successful ambusher “chooses one of the players who voted for them”; “They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: If the player is not a Target, their Ambush fails and they eliminate themselves.
answers.evidence: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, continue with another conspiracy and vote among the survivors.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.” The round is resolved after vote and Ambush effects.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Survivors table: one survivor “collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “Gold Bars are cards, not points”; card values are 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go. They may discuss their intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down; when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; “They may discuss”; each chooses a card face down; “reveal both choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Every player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. The participants in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave all four for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: For zero survivors: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.” Special Rules clarifies final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share player receives zero bars and the Steal player receives all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player takes one bar and the Steal player receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.” The text says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player takes one bar and the Share player receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Share: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one bar, leaving two central. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four.
answers.evidence: “If both choose Grab One & Go, each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round, and give no new gold.”

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: “Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; “If more than one player has reached the threshold, the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: For exactly two qualifying players tied for the highest total, the booklet's instruction is to conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total; one extra Showdown does not end the tie if the highest totals remain tied. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round; stand all IDs upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied highest totals “conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: if no winner, “everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.”

answers.answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including speaking, whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, or texting. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: “roughly a minute and a half at most”; “Any method of communication is allowed, openly or secretly,” including “showing a Voting card, texting”; the game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target player's visible ID color and place it face down in front of yourself. If you want to defend yourself against being the target, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: use “the card matching that player's visible ID color”; each player places one card “face down in front of themselves”; to defend yourself, “play your Ambush card instead.”

answers.answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”

answers.answer: Because all four central bars were awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down for the next round, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Refill: “Deal new central bars face down, keeping their values hidden. If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars.”

answers.answer: No. Blue has the most votes (four versus Purple's three), so Blue is the Target; Blue's successful Ambush protects Blue but does not change who had the most votes or make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target, so they are eliminated (unless protected by a successful Ambush exception).
answers.evidence: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target”; a successful Ambush protects its Target, and “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.” Players who “did not vote for any Target” are eliminated.

answers.answer: The booklet's tie instruction is to conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as needed until there is a single player with the highest total. It does not specify how to arrange a Showdown among more than two tied leaders: the summary says the booklet's card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players, and provides no official multiway procedure.
answers.evidence: Scoring says tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown; source limitation says “its card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players” and “provides no arrangement for three or more players tied.”

answers.answer: Yes. In a double-Steal extra Showdown, every player outside the pair receives one Gold Bar from the deck. The summary expressly says this reward can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.
answers.evidence: “The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can therefore make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.”
